The Old Curiosity Shop. Serialized from 1840 to 1841, this novel follows Little Nell, a young orphan girl, and her grandfather as they are forced to abandon their home and undertake a harrowing journey across England. The cause of their flight is the grandfather's obsession with gambling and games of chance. His addiction destroys the family finances and drives them both into desperation and homelessness. What unfolds is a sentimental and melodramatic tale that combines picaresque adventure with Dickens's growing critique of social exploitation and economic desperation. Little Nell herself is a figure of virtue and innocence, and her sufferings as she wanders homeless across England expose the vulnerability of the orphaned and the poor. Her grandfather, Grandfather Trent, becomes a tragic figure himself, consumed by his gambling addiction even as it destroys everyone around him. Hunting them relentlessly is Daniel Quilp, a grotesque dwarf and scheming moneylender who embodies predatory capitalism. Quilp hounds Nell and her grandfather without mercy, and he carries with him an element of sexual menace that darkens the narrative. Nell's tragic death in the countryside became famous—Victorian readers wept openly when it was serialized. Her death stands as one of Dickens's most emotionally manipulative scenes, and it became the emotional center of public discourse when the novel was published. The novel is also famous for the Old Curiosity Shop itself, a ramshackle antique dealer's store filled with a jumble of artifacts. This setting becomes a symbol of the novel's exploration of loss, ruin, and the past.
